components.name: Admin/Content API key secret generation (via @tryghost/security wrapper)

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Ghost's RSA signing-key generation, both production sites RSA-2048 PKCS#1 PEM: settings.js:37 (legacy keypair generator for members/ghost keys, modulusLength 2048 literal) and signing-key-service.ts:121 (current signing-key service, modulusLength: MIN_MODULUS_LENGTH = 2048 defined at line 94; the service also refuses to load any active key below 2048 bits). These keypairs sign the member and staff JWTs (RS256) and publish to JWKS. RSA-2048 is classically adequate but Shor-vulnerable: signatures

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: the sites declare bcrypt-pbkdf@1.0.2 (not bcrypt itself) in pnpm-lock.yaml — the bcrypt-based KDF cross-implementation typically pulled in via sshpk for encrypted OpenSSH key parsing. The build ships a bcrypt-family PBKDF even though no first-party call site exists in this repo; parameters live inside the consuming dependency.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Ghost's timing-safe comparison layer: token/MAC verification in the admin-toolbar middleware, single-use member tokens, and the shared helper used across services. These are the comparison sites that defend the HMAC-signed magic-link and session tokens against timing oracles. Quantum-safe posture control, kept as the reference implementation for the HMAC assets in this inventory.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: Ed25519 capability ships via tweetnacl@0.14.5 (which provides Ed25519 signatures, X25519 DH and XSalsa20-Poly1305) declared in pnpm-lock.yaml. Ed25519 signatures are Shor-vulnerable long-term but not harvestable. No first-party call site found in this repo; the surface exists in the shipped bundle. Same underlying package as LIB-0469707e (tweetnacl) and the XSalsa20-Poly1305 object.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: jose is a declared dependency of ghost/core (ghost/core/package.json) and is genuinely imported in first-party code: ghost/core/core/server/lib/public-jwk.ts (JWK export of the RSA signing keys for JWKS publishing) plus tests (identities.test.js, editor-settings-authors.acceptance.test.tsx). This is the JOSE/JWK layer of Ghost's JWT infrastructure; its algorithm choices follow the RSA-2048 signing keys it formats. Real library in active use.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: jsonwebtoken is a declared dependency of ghost/core (ghost/core/package.json), imported in 14 files including production code: scheduling/utils.ts (JWT sign for scheduler), api/endpoints/featurebase.js, services/auth/api-key/admin.js, services/members/members-api/services/token-service.js (member session tokens), plus bin/generate-golden-email.js and tests. The JWT algorithms it runs (HS256/RS256) are recorded in the JWT objects of this inventory; this entry is the library itself.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: the legacy `https` npm stub (v1.0.0) is declared in pnpm-lock.yaml — a shim that re-exports Node's https module (TLS 1.2/1.3 via OpenSSL). Pulls the TLS transport surface into the shipped bundle; actual TLS posture is decided by the Node runtime (22.23.3 here), not this package. No first-party TLS cipher configuration found in this repo.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: ssh2@1.17.0 (SSH2 client/server protocol library, incl. SFTP) is declared in pnpm-lock.yaml, likely via the sodo-search or storage tooling. SSH key exchange here is classical (curve25519-sha256, ecdh-* kex) — quantum-vulnerable for recorded sessions long-term. No first-party ssh2 call site found by the collector; the capability ships in the bundle. Observable here, changeable via the dependency version.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: jws@3.2.3 (JSON Web Signature implementation) declared in pnpm-lock.yaml — the signing layer beneath jsonwebtoken, used by Ghost's JWT token services. JWS with HS256/RS256 is quantum-relevant: RSA-signed tokens are forgeable once Shor applies. Same stack as LIB-80a3ff60 (jsonwebtoken) and LIB-9d851bd4 (jws).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: jwa@1.4.2 (JWA algorithm implementations: HS256, RS256, etc.) declared in pnpm-lock.yaml — the primitive layer beneath jws/jsonwebtoken. Shipped bundle carries the JWA algorithm set; first-party JWT use goes through jsonwebtoken/jose instead.

properties.name: pqs:context
